§4.4 Document Type

📚 Document rule — needs other pages of the document; decided once and applied on every page

document-document-type · rule document layout

✅ Normative

Whether a document is a slide deck or a paged document, and which sheet is its cover, MUST be decided once from the whole document and applied to every page. Only the cover MAY carry a Title element.

Two decisions change how single pages are read, and neither can be made from one page:

Decision How it is recognised What it changes on every page
Slide deck or paged document A deck is landscape sheets with one title per sheet, each sheet a self-contained slide. In a deck every slide title is a top-level heading; in a paged document depth carries over page breaks. See Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5.
Which sheet is the cover The title or front page: the document's own name set large, often with authors, a date or a logo, and no body text. Only the cover carries the Title class and the document title. The same words on a later page are page furniture or Text. 
sheet 1  QUARTERLY RESERVING REVIEW       ← cover: Title
sheet 2  Quarterly Reserving Review · 2   ← running header: furniture, not Title

Requirements

  • The decisions MUST be made from the document, not from one sheet. A landscape page on its own does not make a deck — reports insert landscape tables — and the largest line on sheet 1 is not a title if sheet 1 is a transmittal letter.
  • A document with no cover MUST NOT have a Title element anywhere. The first heading MUST NOT be promoted to fill the gap — that is the never invent failure.
  • The same words printed on a later sheet MUST NOT be a Title element; they are page furniture or Text.

Mixed documents

A report with a slide deck appended, or a deck with printed appendix pages, MUST be decided per part. The boundary between the parts is where the decision changes, and each decision MUST be applied to its whole part rather than sheet by sheet.

A single page

Where only one page is available, neither decision can be made. The page MUST be treated as a paged document with no cover: no Title element, and any title-sized line rendered as a heading at the depth the page itself supports.
